hypothesis: KataGo-style terminal ownership supervision improves Go strength per real self-play move and useful neural evaluation.
intervention: Only ownership coefficient: 0.0 vs 1.5. Identical initial parameter trees, scoring, model, root searches, replay, learner schedule and CPU sets.
primary_evidence: Paired-color real matches versus the pinned official 9x9 KataGo checkpoint at 1 and 16 visits after the fixed training budget. Each level uses openings [] and [C3,G7] (4 games per level per arm). Always retain failures, draw scores, exact boards and point margins.
secondary_evidence: training loss curves (different self-play distributions; diagnostic only)
useful neural evaluations, real moves and terminal rows
wall time and process CPU time; compiler FLOP estimates are not MFU
interpretation: One-seed exploratory pilot, not a statistical confirmation or sample-efficiency claim. Two opening pairs are only a functional strength screen; a zero-win floor is inconclusive. Follow with independent seeds and expanded paired panels before selecting an algorithm.
scope: Ownership is a KataGo component control; this does not reproduce its complete training procedure. No KataGo weights or evaluation labels enter training.
